text: Most heart attacks come from a clot blocking an artery, and DMSO slows clotting: it did in mice, and in human platelets (the blood cells that start clots) in a dish. In rats given it for three days before a heart attack, about three quarters less heart muscle died, though they weren't given it after the attack started. That's all animal and lab-dish research so far.
reader: a friend whose companion on a drug has chest pain, deciding whether DMSO with magnesium chloride on the chest is worth using before the next paragraph tells them when to call medics
